expect_red: ...and no state has quietly fallen back to the unstyled border

mutations.contract: Rolling the annotator rail's words into one hover badge did NOT take the colour off the row: each binding state is still distinguishable at a glance, without hovering anything.
mutations.note: Jeff asked to "keep the *color* signal on the row" while collapsing the words, so the colour moved from a word-bearing badge to the row's own left border. That makes a deleted CSS rule a silent loss of the at-a-glance signal -- the rows would still render, still be clickable, and simply stop saying anything. The mutation neutralises one state's colour; the check compares all three, so it cannot be satisfied by a stylesheet that colours them all the same. The witness is a state falling back to `.el-row`'s own neutral border, and the DISTINCTNESS check cannot see that -- the neutral is a fourth colour, so a state that lost its rule stays distinct from the other two while saying nothing. Found by this runner; the suite gained a check that compares each stripe against a clone stripped of its state class.
